Sets the gain out of the amp model, from silence to double, after which the signal is limited to 7.5V either way
Sets the level below which the noise gate closes, -80dB to 0dB
Sets how quickly the gate opens once the signal rises past the threshold, 0.1ms to 50ms
Sets how quickly the gate closes once the hold time has run out, 10ms to 500ms
Sets how long the gate stays open after the signal drops below the threshold, 10ms to 500ms

A peaking filter at 650Hz on the model's output, 12dB of cut fully anticlockwise and 12dB of boost fully clockwise, flat in the middle

Menu — Bundled Models — lists the model files that ship with the plugin; picking one loads it
Menu — Load Custom Model... — opens a file dialogue for a .nam model file anywhere on disk
Menu — Unload Model — drops the loaded model, leaving the module passing its input through
Menu — Eco Mode: Off, On — averages each pair of samples and runs the model once per pair, for about half the processor cost
Menu — Use Fast Tanh — computes the model's activation function from an approximation rather than the library function, for less processor cost
Menu — Waveform Color: Green, Baby Blue, Amber, Red, Purple, White — sets the colour of the bars in the output display
Note — the module passes its input through with the two level knobs applied and nothing else until a model is loaded from the right-click menu
Note — every CV input here replaces its knob rather than adding to it: while a cable is patched, -5V to 5V covers the whole range of that control and the knob is out of circuit
Note — the display across the top is a bar meter of the output signal, and it prints ECO ON in the corner while Eco Mode is on
Note — the green lamp lights when a model is loaded and glows at half brightness while one is loading
Note — the yellow lamp lights when the loaded model was captured at a different sample rate from the engine, which is resampled to match
Note — the red lamp lights while the noise gate is closed
Note — the NAM FX Loop expander goes immediately to the right of this module and inserts its send and return between the amp model and this module's output jack

NamPlayer.notes: The equaliser is applied after the amp model, not before it (src/dsp/Nam.h:215-223). The noise gate and equaliser settings are read once per 128-sample block rather than every sample (src/NamPlayer.cpp:127), so a fast CV into any of those nine jacks is quantized to that block. Model loading happens on a background thread, so the module keeps passing audio while a large model loads.

Fades between the signal the NAM Player sent and the signal arriving at the return jack, all send fully anticlockwise and all return fully clockwise
Whatever the NAM Player would otherwise have put out, for patching into an effect; it carries 0V when this module is not touching a NAM Player
The effect's output coming back; unpatched, the sent signal is used in its place, so the blend control then has nothing to fade between
Note — the blended result does not come out of this module: it goes back through the expander connection and out of the NAM Player's own output jack
Note — the green lamp lights while a NAM Player is immediately to the left of this module
Note — placed anywhere else, the send carries 0V and the return is ignored

lines: Cabinet simulator: it convolves a mono signal with up to two impulse responses loaded from WAV files, fades between them, and puts a high-pass and a low-pass filter on the result
With both impulse responses loaded, fades from the first fully anticlockwise to the second fully clockwise; with only one loaded, fades from the unprocessed signal to the convolved one
Sets the corner of the 2-pole low-pass filter on the output, 1000Hz fully anticlockwise to 20000Hz fully clockwise, on a logarithmic scale
Sets the corner of the 2-pole high-pass filter on the output, 20Hz fully anticlockwise to 2000Hz fully clockwise, on a logarithmic scale
Sets the output gain, from silence to double
The signal to be convolved, mono, with 5V taken as full scale
Takes over the BLEND control while patched, -5V for one end of the fade and 5V for the other; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the LP corner while patched, -5V for 1000Hz and 5V for 20000Hz; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the HP corner while patched, -5V for 20Hz and 5V for 2000Hz; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
Takes over the output gain while patched, -5V for silence and 5V for double; the knob does nothing while a cable is in here
The filtered, convolved signal, mono

Menu — Unload IR A — empties the first slot, greyed out when nothing is in it

Note — the menu prints a line under the two slots saying what the blend control is doing: a crossfade between the two responses when both are loaded, or a dry-to-wet fade when only one is

CabSim.notes: The convolution runs in 256-sample blocks, so the blend is applied once per block rather than per sample (src/dsp/CabSimDSP.h:189-192); the two filters run per sample. The filter corners are recomputed only when they move by more than 1Hz (src/CabSim.cpp:111-116), so very small CV movements do not retune them. Rack's own bypass is configured to pass the input jack to the output jack.

lines: Bucket-brigade delay modelled on an analogue memory delay pedal, with chorus and vibrato modulation of the delay clock, a compander, and the hiss and clock bleed of the original circuit
Sets the drive into the modelled preamp and compander, so higher settings add saturation before the delay
Fades between the direct signal and the delayed one, on a law that lifts the middle so the level does not drop there
Sets how much of the delayed signal is returned to the input for repeats; high settings bloom into self-oscillation
Sets the delay time by setting the bucket-brigade clock period, about 33ms fully anticlockwise to about 410ms fully clockwise, or 819ms in the long range; moving it bends the repeats
Sets how far the chorus or vibrato modulation moves the delay clock
Scales the Level CV input before it is added to the LEVEL knob, backwards at negative settings
Scales the Blend CV input before it is added to the BLEND knob, backwards at negative settings
Scales the Feedback CV input before it is added to the FEED knob, backwards at negative settings
Scales the Delay CV input before it is added to the delay time, backwards at negative settings
Scales the Depth CV input before it is added to the DEPTH knob, backwards at negative settings
Chooses chorus or vibrato: chorus modulates at about 0.35Hz in the middle of the delay range and vibrato at about 1.65Hz, and shorter delay times raise both
Chooses the modulation wave, a triangle in one position and a square in the other; the square steps the delay time between two values
Doubles the longest delay time, from about 410ms to about 819ms
Engages the effect in the upper position and bypasses it in the lower, despite the panel printing BYPASS beside it; bypassed, the input comes out untouched
Adds to the LEVEL knob after the trimpot for this jack scales it, 5V covering the whole range at a trimpot fully clockwise
Adds to the BLEND knob after the trimpot for this jack scales it, 5V covering the whole range at a trimpot fully clockwise
Adds to the FEED knob after the trimpot for this jack scales it, 5V covering the whole range at a trimpot fully clockwise
Adds to the delay time after the trimpot for this jack scales it, 5V covering the whole range at a trimpot fully clockwise, whether the knob or the tapped tempo is setting that time
Adds to the DEPTH knob after the trimpot for this jack scales it, 5V covering the whole range at a trimpot fully clockwise
Chooses vibrato above 1V and chorus below it while patched, in place of the CH/VB switch
Chooses the square modulation wave above 1V and the triangle below it while patched, in place of the TRI/SQ switch
Chooses the long delay range above 1V and the normal range below it while patched, in place of the RANGE switch
Engages the effect above 1V and bypasses it below while patched, in place of the BYPASS switch
Sets the delay time from the interval between rising edges above 2V, taking taps between 0.08 and 4 seconds apart, and switches the menu's Timing to the tapped setting
The signal to be delayed; each channel of a polyphonic cable gets its own delay engine, up to sixteen
The direct and delayed signals mixed by the BLEND control, one channel per input channel, or two when a mono input is spread by one of the stereo modes
The input signal passed through untouched, for parallel patching
The delayed signal on its own, before the BLEND control
The LEVEL control's value after its CV and trimpot, as 0V to 10V
The BLEND control's value after its CV and trimpot, as 0V to 10V
The FEED control's value after its CV and trimpot, as 0V to 10V
The delay time as a proportion of the current range after its CV and trimpot, as 0V to 10V
The DEPTH control's value after its CV and trimpot, as 0V to 10V
10V while vibrato is chosen and 0V while chorus is
The modulation wave itself, triangle or square as chosen, swinging between -5V and 5V
10V while the long delay range is chosen and 0V while the normal range is
10V while the effect is engaged and 0V while it is bypassed
A square wave at the bucket-brigade clock divided by 64, switching between 0V and 10V, so it speeds up as the delay time shortens
A square wave at the bucket-brigade clock divided by 512, switching between 0V and 10V, so it speeds up as the delay time shortens
The modelled compander's envelope as 0V to 10V, rising with the level going into the delay
Menu — Artifact profile: Cleaner BBD, Rev_D authentic, Worn unit — sets how much hiss, clock bleed and drift the delay adds
Menu — Bypass behavior: Trails, CPU mute — chooses whether the delay memory keeps running while the effect is bypassed, or is cleared and the processing skipped
Menu — Timing: Free delay knob, Tap/sync delay — chooses whether the DELAY knob sets the time or the tapped tempo and division do
Menu — Division: 1/1, 1/2, 1/4., 1/4, 1/8., 1/8, 1/8T, 1/16 — on the Timing submenu, sets the note value of the tapped tempo that the delay time takes
Menu — Tap tempo seed: 60 BPM, 90 BPM, 120 BPM, 140 BPM — on the Timing submenu, sets a tempo without tapping and switches Timing to the tapped setting
Menu — Stereo mode: Mono pedal, Wide chorus, Ping-pong offset — chooses whether a mono input is spread over two channels, and how far the second channel's delay and modulation are offset
Menu — Advanced calibration — seven trims over input gain, bucket-brigade bias, clock bleed, compander, noise, wet makeup and feedback headroom, each from off to 200 per cent of normal
Menu — Reset calibration trims — returns all seven calibration trims to 100 per cent
Menu — Clear delay memory — empties the delay buffer, cutting off repeats and any self-oscillation
Note — the DELAY knob does nothing while the menu's Timing is set to Tap/sync delay: the tapped tempo and division set the time, and the Delay CV is added to that
Note — a stereo mode other than Mono pedal spreads a mono input over two channels only while the effect is engaged
Note — tapping the Tap input switches the menu's Timing to Tap/sync delay on its own, which takes the DELAY knob out of circuit

Mnemonix.notes: The delay figures come from the clock constants at src/dsp/MnemonixDSP.h:280-283: 4096 bucket-brigade stages at a clock period of 8 to 100 microseconds, or 8 to 200 in the long range, giving 32.768ms to 409.6ms and 819.2ms. The LFO, clock and envelope outputs are taken from the first channel only, even when the audio is polyphonic (src/Mnemonix.cpp:285-291). The four gate outputs and the five control-value outputs are written only while something is patched to them. The panel prints BYPASS beside the engage switch, while the switch's own tooltip reads Effect with positions Bypassed and Engaged, and the upper position is Engaged.
